decision: Hillclimb: make the Metal engine 30 percent faster with no loss of quality, experiments fanned out to a swarm, one GPU run at a time
why: the user asked for it; the one-process rule from 2026-10-18 still holds

decision: Metric: GPU ms per decode frame, the rows-1 backbone plus tower line of drama bench on the tuned schedule, median of 5 interleaved runs; secondary: end-to-end frames/s of the 600-frame perf_ab generation. Target 14.6 ms (30 percent under 20.8). Stop: target met and at least 8 attempts, or no cheap hypothesis left. Quality: compare.py within eval/thresholds.json against the float32 oracle dump with top-1 1.0, frames byte-identical or the e2e suite unchanged
why: decode is what a listener waits on; prefill is already one pass

decision: Tuned bench on main 1a5993e, app quit, load about 3: backbone one row 14.8 ms, tower 6.0 ms; profile rows 1 sums to 10.4 ms cache-warm (linear.gemm.qkv 2.1, moe.gateup 1.6, moe.down 1.0, full.gemm.qkv 0.9, linear.gemm.out 0.9, moe.shared 0.8, linear.gemm.z 0.8, router+bucket 0.7)
why: one run each before the harness is frozen; the A/A noise run follows

decision: Bytes per decode frame from the config: dense bf16 backbone about 2.55 GB, FP8 experts plus scales about 1.8 GB, tower bf16 about 1.95 GB, 6.3 GB in all, so 20.8 ms is about 300 GB/s on a 400 GB/s part; 30 percent less time needs 430 GB/s, past the hardware, so the target needs fewer bytes per frame, and the only quality-neutral way is lossless weight compression; kernel efficiency alone tops out near 15 to 20 percent
why: arithmetic before hypotheses, so the swarm attacks bytes as well as bandwidth

decision: tools/with-gpu-lock serializes every timed GPU run and model load through one flock; every worker and delegate runs drama, kbench and model-loading tests through it
why: the rule lived in briefs and was broken once; a lock cannot be forgotten
